source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1032 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1032 was established by Ordinance No. 31555, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 10, 2020. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1032 is established on property located on the north line of Hale Street east of Dwight Avenue. The size of PD 1032 is approximately 4.85 acres. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) STOOP means a small porch leading to the entrance of a residence.

(2) TANDEM PARKING means one parking space in front of another parking space, making it necessary to pass through one parking space to gain vehicular access to the other parking space.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 1032A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 1032A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For single family and handicapped group dwelling units and accessory community center (private) uses, development and use of the Property must comply with a subdivision plat. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and a subdivision plat, the text of this article controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District is subject to DIR in this district; etc. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory use is permitted by right.

-- Accessory community center (private). (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the TH-2(A) Townhouse District apply.

(b) Setbacks.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this subsection, no front, side, or rear setbacks are required.

(2) Hale Street. Minimum setback is 15 feet. Balconies, stoops, awnings, cantilevered roof eaves, stairs, steps, and other architectural features may encroach up to five feet into the required setback.

(c) Density. For single family and handicapped group dwelling unit uses, maximum number of dwelling units is 39.

(d) Height. For single family and handicapped group dwelling unit uses, maximum structure height is 30 feet.

(e) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 75 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculation; surface parking lots, underground parking structures, and unenclosed structures are not. For a shared access development, the shared access area may be used to determine lot coverage. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Single family and handicapped group dwelling unit.

(1) A minimum of 0.30 spaces per dwelling unit and two spaces per lot must be provided on the Property for guest parking. Guest parking may be provided in the shared access area as shown on the conceptual plan.

(2) Assigned parking spaces may be provided as tandem parking. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Shared access development with more than 36 lots.

(1) Open space. A minimum of 20 percent of the Property must be maintained as open space. Flood plain areas may be used to meet the open space requirement. A pedestrian trail is required in the open space area along the western portion of the property, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(2) Pedestrian and bicycle amenities. A minimum of two of each of the following pedestrian and bicycle amenities must be provided within the open space along the western portion of the property, as shown on the conceptual plan:

(A) benches;

(B) trash receptacle; and

(C) bicycle racks.

(c) Plant materials. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Shared Access Development
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.113. SHARED ACCESS DEVELOPMENT.

(a) A shared access development may have a maximum of 39 individual lots on a single plat.

(b) A shared access area may serve no more than 39 dwelling units per shared access point.

(c) A shared access development may be completed by a phased final plat. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.114. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31555)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1032.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31555)
